title: Sensitive Data Retention & Pseudonymization Playbook — Enterprise Onboarding
author: Samantha Lee
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the recommended end-to-end handling of customer-sensitive data for enterprise customers during onboarding and recurring operations. It focuses on: retention policy mapping, pseudonymization approaches we support across deployment modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), request and audit flows, verification steps for handback, and escalation paths for data incidents. Follow this playbook when a customer requires contractual controls over retention, deletion, or partial pseudonymization for compliance (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, sector regulations).

When to use this playbook
- New enterprise customers whose contract or security questionnaire includes data retention/deletion obligations.
- Customers requesting pseudonymization or reversible tokenization for specific data classes.
- During migrations or cutovers where data residency or retention windows change.

Owner & SLA targets
- Document owner: Customer Success (Samantha Lee)
- Technical owner: Platform Security (Diego Alvarez)
- Oncall escalation: Security oncall (rotation – see Security runbook)
- Target SLAs for requests originating from the customer security contact:
  1) Acknowledgement: within 4 business hours.
  2) Technical plan (for retention/pseudonymization changes): 48 business hours.
  3) Completed reversible pseudonymization request (up to 5M records): 7 business days.
  4) Full deletion requests (hosted metadata + cached keys): 48 hours for Hosted; 5 business days for Dedicated; customer-managed in Private (support assists with playbook).

Data classification matrix
| Customer data class | Typical location | Recommended treatment | Retention default | Notes |
|---------------------|------------------|-----------------------|-------------------|-------|
| PII (names, emails) | Request body, logs (redacted) | Pseudonymize + encrypted at rest | 365 days (configurable) | PII in logs must be redacted at ingestion
| Generated text (user prompts + responses) | Model input/output, cache zones | Respect customer policy: retain or delete on request | 180 days default | KV cache TTL configurable per customer
| Auth tokens & API keys | Secrets store / KMS | Never stored in plain form; rotate per policy | 90 days | Redwood does not index plaintext tokens
| Audit logs & traces | Observability backend | Aggregated and low-cardinality retention | 365 days | High-frequency logs sampled to meet cost SLOs

Architectural options and implications
- Hosted API: Redwood controls retention/keys; fastest path for contractual deletion. Provide retention profile in contract (standard/short/strict).
- Dedicated: Redwood-managed infra for customer; we operate deletion tools but must coordinate with Reserved Capacity Ops. Deletion time windows are longer due to bulk processing.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer controls primary data plane; Redwood provides step-by-step scripts and verification checks for data erasure.

Selection guidelines
1) If customer requires sub-48-hour deletion, recommend Hosted with strict retention profile.
2) If customer requires on-prem isolation but needs Redwood assistance for migration, document reversible pseudonymization approach during handoff.

Operational request flow (high level)
1. Customer raises a retention/pseudonymization/deletion request through their designated CS contact or Support portal (ticket).
2. CS triages: confirm customer identity, scope (IDs, time window, data classes), and desired outcome (delete vs pseudonymize vs export).
3. CS opens a JIRA (tag: data-retention) and attaches signed authorization if required by contract.
4. Platform Security reviews and approves technical plan.
5. Ops executes plan in sandbox then prod.
6. Verification report produced and shared with customer; ticket closed after sign-off.

Detailed runbook: delete request example (Hosted)
1) Intake & validation
   - Required fields from customer: customer_id, record_ids OR retention window (ISO8601), contact email, signed auth (if contract requires).
   - Validate ticket owner against contract SSO groups.
2) Prepare rollback-safe snapshot (if requested by customer)
   - For Hosted, take a filtered snapshot of metadata only (no secrets) and store in retention vault for 30 days unless customer declines.
3) Execute pseudonymization or deletion
   - Use the data management tool (internal CLI: redwood-datactl) with dry-run first.
   - Sample command (dry-run):
     redwood-datactl delete --customer 12345 --window 2024-01-01:2024-12-31 --dry-run
   - Production run:
     redwood-datactl delete --customer 12345 --window 2024-01-01:2024-12-31 --confirm --audit=case-789
4) KV cache considerations
   - Invalidate affected KV cache prefixes and trigger background eviction if large.
   - Confirm no long-lived prefixes remain for pseudonymized records.
5) Post-process & verification
   - Run verification query to confirm zero results for scoped identifiers.
   - Generate signed verification report including run ids, hashes of affected record ids, and operator audit trail.

Escalation ladder (data handling incidents)
1) Customer Success Engineer (first responder) — <cs-oncall>@redwood.com — 4h SLA for acknowledgement.
2) Platform Security — sec-oncall@redwood.com — 2 business-hour escalation for suspected exposure.
3) Dedicated Ops Lead — ops-dedicated@redwood.com — for capacity/throughput constraints impacting deletion windows.
4) VP Customer Success — vp-cs@redwood.com — for contractual disputes or regulatory notices.

Verification checklist (required before closing ticket)
- [ ] Authorization verified and attached to ticket.
- [ ] Dry-run executed and approved by Platform Security.
- [ ] Production run complete; job IDs and timestamps recorded.
- [ ] KV cache invalidated and redis/edge eviction confirmed.
- [ ] Verification report generated and signed.
- [ ] Customer acknowledgment received or 7-day silent acceptance elapsed.

Sample pseudonymization approach (reversible tokenization)
- Tokenization step: replace sensitive fields with reversible token stored in a customer-scoped, envelope-encrypted store (KMS-wrapped).
- Token format example (JSON):
  {
    \"token\": \"tok_3G6aZ...\",
    \"method\": \"aes-gcm-kms\",
    \"kms_key_id\": \"projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/enterprise/cryptoKeys/ent-2025\"
  }
- Controls: token access requires explicit ACL entry and MUST be logged to audit trail.

Example API request for deletion (customer-facing support assist)
- Customer can initiate a scoped export or deletion via the Support portal or API (if enabled in contract). Example curl (support agent acting on behalf):
  curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/customers/12345/actions/delete\" \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_TOKEN\" \
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
    -d '{\"scope\": {\"from\":\"2025-01-01\",\"to\":\"2025-06-30\"}, \"data_classes\":[\"generated_text\",\"pii\"], \"signed_auth\":\"<base64-pdf>\"}'

Telemetry & observability requirements
- Every retention/pseudonymization job MUST emit the following fields to the data-management metrics stream:
  - job_id, customer_id, operator, job_type (delete/pseudonymize/export), affected_count, start_ts, end_ts, outcome (success/partial/failure), verification_hash
- Alerting thresholds: failure rate > 3% across jobs in 24h window triggers an Ops incident.

Legal & compliance artifacts (required per enterprise contract)
- Signed Data Processing Addendum (DPA) with retention table
- Signed scope authorization for each deletion request (if outside DPA windows)
- Verification report (PDF) with audit hashes and operator signatures

Common failure modes & workarounds
- Large-volume deletion timeouts: schedule batched deletes during low-traffic windows and use background streaming deletions.
- Stale KV cache keys: force eviction and increment cache prefix version for affected customer.
- Missing authorization: route to CS Legal for expedited approval after identity proofing.

FAQ
Q: Can Redwood restore deleted data after a customer deletes?
A: For Hosted and Dedicated, Redwood maintains an optional short-lived snapshot only if customer requests a rollback window; otherwise deletion is irreversible after verification report. For Private, restoration depends on customer backups.

Appendix A — Example verification report outline
- Header: customer_id, case_id, operator, date
- Scope: retention window, data classes
- Execution summary: job_id, nodes used, duration, affected_count
- Hash table: list of hashed identifiers confirming deletion (salted hashing scheme)
- Signatures: operator and Platform Security approver
